old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a bowl filled with a dark liquid, placed on a white surface. Two wooden sticks are partially submerged in the liquid, positioned at an angle across the bowl. A second stick enters the frame and becomes fully submerged by the end of the sequence. The camera exhibits a slight, continuous downward tilt over time, altering the perspective of the bowl's rim and background. The lighting is consistent, highlighting the color of the liquid and the texture of the wooden sticks. The liquid's surface shows visible deformation and color gradient changes as the sticks are manipulated, indicating a dynamic process. The overall composition emphasizes the stillness and simplicity of the scene, with the addition of the second stick and camera movement introducing subtle changes.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a bowl filled with a dark red liquid, likely a sauce or soup, placed on a white surface. Two wooden sticks are partially submerged in the liquid, positioned at an angle across the bowl. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the bowl and its contents. The lighting is consistent, highlighting the rich color of the liquid and the texture of the wooden sticks. There are no visible changes in the position of the sticks or any other objects within the frame, suggesting a static scene without any movement or action occurring. The overall composition emphasizes the stillness and simplicity of the scene.
caption: The video captures a close, slightly tilted overhead view of a white dish holding dark reddish-brown liquid streaked with orange-yellow swirls. Three pale wooden craft sticks already rest in the liquid: one angled down-left with a rounded white paddle end, one short vertical stick in the center, and one angled down-right forming a V over the brightest orange area. A small pink smudge sits on the dry white surface at the upper left. The sticks remain in the same positions throughout, with no lifting, insertion, or stirring visible. The orange boundary shifts slowly, and the right stick becomes visible as a wider flat paddle outline rather than a thin bright line. The framing stays on the same region, with the dish edge and smudge holding their positions.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless

collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
